Generating long content with LLMs presents a challenge due to the substantial memory requirements of the transient state, known as the key-value (KV) cache, which scales with sequence length and batch size. This blog reviews InfiniGen, a novel KV cache management framework designed specifically for long-text generation, which integrates seamlessly with modern offloading-based inference systems, which leverage larger CPU memory. InfiniGen leverages a key insight: only a few essential tokens are [...] tokens are necessary to compute the attention layers of Transformers in subsequent steps. By speculating on these critical tokens using the inputs of the current layer and part of the query weight and key cache of the next layer, InfiniGen enables prefetching of only the essential KV cache entries, thus reducing fetch overhead from host CPU memory in offloading-based LLM systems. We present InfiniGen, a dynamic KV cache management framework that
synergistically works with modern offloading-based LLM serving systems by

synergistically work with modern offloading-based inference systems.
InfiniGen builds on two key design principles.

produce the next output token, dropping the non-critical ones, by conducting a

can effectively reduce the KV cache transfer overhead while preserving model
accuracy.

# InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management

## Abstract

InfiniGen is a KV cache management framework that improves performance and accuracy in long-text generation by pre-fetching essential KV cache entries in offloading-based LLM serving systems. [...] fetching them all), thereby mitigating the fetch overhead from the host memory
in offloading-based LLM serving systems. Our evaluation on several
representative LLMs shows that InfiniGen improves the overall performance of a
modern offloading-based system by up to 3.00x compared to prior KV cache
management methods while offering substantially better model accuracy.
